adrs.title: Catalogue data lives as one JSON file per service
A deprecated dependency warns; it does not block an onboarding plan
Cost and chargeback are out of scope for v1

decisions.decision: Catalogue content is illustrative, in data files separate from code
Full site in one pass; library still testable standalone
Design quality is a delivery requirement
Composite = product over target + transitive closure, each service once; contribution `1-(1-a)^N`, N absent ⇒ 1, instance failures independent
decisions.rationale: Fixed, testable formula with exact fixtures — **but an author-chosen model (PRD A-2), confirmed at the plan gate, see ledger row 6**

decisions.decision: One JSON file per service, schema-validated at build; discovered by `import.meta.glob`
decisions.rationale: No front-matter pipeline; clear ownership; editable without TS

decisions.decision: Site passes `advisory` deprecation policy; library requires the parameter and supports `blocking` too
decisions.rationale: Brief: "know, and have the migration path"; blocking makes the catalogue unusable when a foundation deprecates

decisions.decision: Cost/chargeback out of scope for v1
decisions.rationale: Reversible direction; different owner and cadence

decisions.decision: Canonical term is **availability**; "SLA" is a glossary alias in the UI only. Module is `availability.ts`, not `sla.ts`
decisions.rationale: PRD uses "availability"; the API must not carry the overloaded word

decisions.decision: Eligibility vocabularies live in **data** as `schema.json` enums, and eligibility is a **set-membership** test: a service lists the classifications and tiers it accepts and the controls it requires; a team profile carries one classification, one tier, and its attested controls. `types.ts` types both dimensions as plain `string` (applied in the working tree); the PBI-002 drift test validates a typed sample against the schema's *structure*, never enum equality; PBI-010's profile picker reads the enum values from `catalogue/schema.json` at build time (read-only dependency)
decisions.rationale: PRD A-16 default; keeps vocabulary editable without TypeScript (C-5) — a real-vocabulary change is a data + schema edit only; no ordering assumption baked into logic

decisions.decision: **Routing and offline model:** hash-based routing; `import.meta.glob(..., { eager: true })`; a single JS bundle with no dynamic imports; **no service worker** in v1. In-session navigation after first load is proven **by construction** (AC-25's static scan + the single bundle + fonts preloaded on first load); an offline *reload* is not supported — a narrowing of PRD S-5/C-1 recorded in Out-of-scope
decisions.rationale: GitHub Pages project paths break history routing on deep links; lazy chunks fail offline; a SW is a separate operational commitment

decisions.decision: **Test harness split:** Vitest `projects` — `lib` (node, `src/lib/**/*.test.ts`, no DOM) and `ui` (`happy-dom`, `src/ui/**/*.test.ts`); `axe-core` runs inside the `ui` project **with `color-contrast` excluded** (happy-dom performs no layout, so that rule returns *incomplete*); NFR-9 contrast is discharged by PBI-008's token-contrast test instead. Layout-dependent checks (AC-32 viewports; network-disabled navigation) are a **manual owner gate** on the deployed build, like NFR-4
decisions.rationale: PRD NFR-6 forbids DOM emulation in the library suite while AC-31/34/36/37 need a DOM; no real-browser harness is in the dependency list

decisions.decision: **Result types are module-local** (`availability.ts` owns `Working`, `eligibility.ts` owns `EligibilityResult`, etc.); `types.ts` owns only the data model, `Result`, and the shared error types; `src/lib/index.ts` is created **only** by PBI-007
decisions.rationale: Lets PBI-003/004/005 run in parallel without touching a shared file

decisions.decision: **Fixtures F1–F6 are test-only** and owned by PBI-001 at `src/lib/testing/fixtures.ts`; F1 reuses catalogue ids with PRD-fixed values that the illustrative catalogue need not match
decisions.rationale: One owner; the PRD values are gate values, not content

decisions.decision: `formatAvailability()` (PRD FR-13) is shipped by PBI-003 in the library; PBI-009 only renders its output
decisions.rationale: The rounding rule is part of the tested computation

decisions.decision: **Dependency additions** (all dev-time; none affects the NFR-3 runtime budget except the three font packages, of which only the **latin subset files** are imported, bundled, and counted): `@tailwindcss/vite` (already installed), `@vitest/coverage-v8`, `happy-dom`, `axe-core`, `ajv` + `ajv-formats`, `@fontsource-variable/bricolage-grotesque`, `@fontsource/ibm-plex-sans`, `@fontsource/ibm-plex-mono`. **No script-runner package:** `scripts/*.ts` run under Node's native type stripping (`node scripts/x.ts`), which requires **Node ≥ 22.18** — pinned by `engines.node` in `package.json` (PBI-000) and to be matched by `setup-node` in PBI-012's workflow; this also satisfies PRD NFR-1's "Node 22" reference environment. Nothing else without a ledger row
